name: CORE — New Database Principal Accessing Core Banking
description:
Attacker objective
Access or manipulate the core-banking database with a new or compromised account — a principal that does not normally touch the core banking schema.

Attack logic
The core-banking database is accessed by a very small, fixed set of service and application principals. A principal not seen before performing any operation against the core banking audit trail is a strong anomaly — a new service account, a misconfiguration, or a compromised/rogue identity reaching the crown-jewel database.

Why this detection works
A new-terms model over the database principal auto-baselines the known core-banking accounts and fires only on a genuinely new one.

False positives
Onboarding of a new legitimate core-banking service/application account.

Tuning
Verify and allowlist new legitimate principals; correlate the new principal's source and the operations it performed against the core banking database.

Required telemetry
Core banking database audit (apps-*, type=CORE_AuditTrail): USERNAME, ACTION_NAME, SQL_TEXT.
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. USERNAME = the new database principal; review ACTION_NAME and SQL_TEXT for what it did.
2. Confirm whether the principal was legitimately onboarded; a new actor on the core banking database is high-risk.
3. Correlate with the source host/application and with any privileged operations.
false_positives: Onboarding of a new legitimate core-banking service/application account.
